question.text: Mandovi Private Credit Fund (Cat II) declares its First Close with total capital commitments of INR 18 crore. Is this First Close valid under SEBI (AIF) Regulations?

answer.text: Yes - First Close can be declared at any commitment level
Yes - if the Sponsor waives its continuing interest
No - at First Close, the corpus shall NOT be less than INR 20 crore minimum prescribed under the AIF Regulations (Social Impact Funds: INR 5 crore)
Yes - if the fund converts to a Special Situation Fund

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI (AIF) Regulations, at the date of declaration of First Close, the corpus of an AIF shall not be less than the prescribed minimum corpus of INR 20 crore (or INR 5 crore for Social Impact Funds). At INR 18 crore the Mandovi fund is below the INR 20 crore floor, so the First Close is not valid. The Trap: Options A and B ignore the prescribed minimum corpus floor. Option D suggests a conversion route that does not relax the First Close corpus rule. Note: The workbook supports the First Close minimum corpus requirement of INR 20 crore for AIFs generally, with INR 5 crore for Social Impact Funds.
